title: POC 2: show one project's tasks, owners and agent discussions
description:
Extend the working native POC page with a read-only view of one explicitly configured local Waystation project. Show the selected project, tasks and statuses, current claim owners, selected task description/acceptance and its canonical agent discussion thread. Supply manual refresh, a last-successful-read indicator, loading/empty/error states and escaped record text. Reuse existing task, claim and message reads through existing CLI/MCP contracts; if a necessary read is absent, add only a narrowly allowlisted adapter over existing core helpers and the read-only lock. Never parse canonical JSON independently in plugin code. Any subprocess uses argument arrays, an explicit fixed ledger root and finite timeout/output limits; data requests cannot override the root or run arbitrary commands. Existing commands have different result shapes, so validate their actual contracts instead of assuming every command returns the same envelope. Use a controlled demo ledger first and verify read-only behavior. This is a small-project, manual-refresh experiment: do not implement polling, cursor infrastructure, versioned snapshots, multiple projects, live Hermes transcripts, commit reconciliation or production session bindings. Report oversized/failed reads explicitly instead of presenting empty or silently truncated data.

If the POC 1 implementation is not present in integrations/hermes/, reconstruct the minimal loading page from the POC 1 acceptance criteria before building the read-only view. Record the reconstruction in the task notes.
acceptance: The native page displays one configured project's tasks, claim owners, task details and canonical discussion messages, with sender, recipient/broadcast, time and body visible.
A task or message change appears after manual refresh; empty data and a failed read look different, and last-good data is visibly stale after failure.
No refresh or navigation changes fixture canonical records/events, claims or status; no composer, assignment control, Kanban card or worker dispatch is introduced.
Root/command injection, missing ledger, timeout, excessive output and untrusted HTML-like message text are handled explicitly and safely by focused tests.
Evidence identifies reusable native UI/read-adapter pieces and the intentionally omitted production guarantees; this does not mark W05 or W08b/W08c done.
notes: Current milestone is the proof of concept in section 0 of docs/waystation-git-hermes-implementation-plan.md. This bounded experiment does not complete or authorize the full W04-W10 implementation. Preserve the user's native Hermes app preference. No agents are dispatched by task creation.
